mainEntity.name: Do you supply products or only introduce factories?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our offer is product sourcing, purchase and supply. The company identified in your quotation contracts with you and invoices the products. Specifications, samples, product pricing and order responsibilities are agreed before you commit.

mainEntity.name: Do you only source clothing and packaging?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clothing, textiles and packaging are our core specialties. We also source other products on request, after reviewing the product, quantity, specifications and production requirements.

mainEntity.name: Can I start a sourcing project now?

mainEntity.name: Can you work from an existing design or sample?

mainEntity.name: Who handles compliance and import requirements?

mainEntity.name: Which company will invoice my order?

Product specifications, pricing, samples, payment terms and delivery responsibilities are agreed for each order. The U.S. expansion remains planned.

mainEntity.name: What is the minimum order quantity?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single minimum order quantity for every product. Materials, construction, finishes and quantities by size, color or artwork affect the proposal. Send your brief so we can review the available options.

pages.content: How Our China Sourcing and Product Supply Process WorksSourcing Lab USA starts with your brief, reviews supplier options and samples, and agrees product pricing, production checkpoints and order responsibilities before purchasing and supplying the goods.What do we supply, and who is it for? Sourcing Lab USA is a custom packaging and textile procurement partner for U.S. brands and business customers. We source, purchase and supply products through an established independent China sourcing partnership. Clothing, textiles, sportswear, packaging and labels are core specialties. Other products are reviewed for feasibility before a proposal is made. Projects can start now. The quotation identifies the company in France or China that contracts with you and invoices the goods. The Miami expansion is planned for 2027. Read about the business and the difference between an agent and a product supply arrangement. What happens between a brief and an order? The process below explains the decisions described in our supply offer. Exact deliverables, checks, timing and responsibilities are agreed for each project. StageWhat is reviewedWhat needs your decisionProduct briefIntended use, specifications, quantity, destination and timingConfirm the requirement and identify unresolved detailsFeasibility and supplier optionsWhether the brief can be proposed through the China partnershipReview proposed options and differencesQuotation and samplesProduct price, sample scope, materials, construction and brandingConfirm the quoted basis and sample approvalsOrder agreementContracting company, specification, quantities, payment and responsibilitiesApprove the written order termsProduction follow-upAgreed checkpoints and changes affecting the orderResolve issues and approve changes where requiredDelivery arrangementsPacking, shipping terms and import responsibilitiesConfirm the agreed handoff and receiving arrangements Submitting a brief requests a discussion; it does not place an order. Prepare your RFQ or send the details you have. How should approvals be documented? Use a product reference and revision throughout the brief, quotation, sample comments and order. Identify which sample features are approved and which require correction. Keep changes to materials, quantities or artwork visible, with the responsible person and date. This gives the buyer and supplying company a common reference for the order. Our supplier evidence matrix and quality checkpoint worksheet are planning resources you can adapt. They are not certificates or evidence that a particular supplier has been audited. What does quality coordination mean? Quality follow-up means production coordination and the checkpoints agreed for the order. It is not an independent certified inspection service. If independent inspection, laboratory testing or technical review is needed, the provider, scope and costs must be identified separately in the project arrangements. A sample approval, a production photograph and a test report answer different questions. Define what each item is intended to establish before relying on it. Product compliance cannot be guaranteed by a generic sourcing checklist. Who handles transport and import responsibilities? Delivery may be direct from China under the agreed commercial terms. The quotation and order must identify the responsibilities for transport, import review and delivery. Sourcing Lab USA does not offer standalone customs brokerage or freight forwarding. Specialist work belongs with the appropriate appointed providers. Compare the landed-cost inputs and China-to-U.S. procurement scope before assuming that an amount includes delivery or import charges. What is useful in the first conversation? Send product references, estimated quantity, intended market, budget basis if available, and the date you are working toward. Tell us if you already have a supplier or sample and which decisions are still open. You can start with a short brief and provide more detail after the scope is discussed. Discuss your sourcing project. Method explained September 14, 2026; specific order terms control the work agreed for your project.

They help readers prepare decisions; they do not certify suppliers, products or import arrangements.Who publishes these resources? Sourcing Lab USA publishes educational material about sourcing and product procurement. The About page identifies the business and its founder. Articles show their attribution and publication date. A named author is used where the article is attributed to that person; organization-attributed planning resources do not imply personal review or endorsement by the founder. AI-assisted drafting is used for some planning resources. Authorship is not a claim that every paragraph comes from firsthand fieldwork. A planning guide, a hypothetical example and a report of an actual project must be clearly distinguished. How are facts and examples presented? Business descriptions follow the stated offer: clothing, textiles and packaging are core specialties, with other products assessed for feasibility. Current projects are contracted and invoiced through the company in France or China identified in the quotation. The Miami expansion is planned for 2027. Original worksheets and frameworks are identified as editorial tools. They do not claim industry recognition, supplier certification or a validated predictive score. Numerical examples are labeled hypothetical and show their assumptions. They are not customer results, quoted prices, market averages or guaranteed savings. Previously published indicative quantity and timing figures are planning references, qualified by product and order conditions. The quotation confirms the figures for an actual order. Which external sources are used? For U.S. import and product questions, resources link to relevant primary authorities such as CBP, USITC, FTC, CPSC and EPA where applicable. Event arrangements are referred to the event organizer; Incoterms guidance is referred to the International Chamber of Commerce. Source links are placed near the statements they support. A date of source checking describes the editorial check, not a promise that rules remain unchanged. Readers should recheck the authority and obtain the appropriate product, legal or customs advice for a real decision. An official link is not an endorsement of Sourcing Lab USA by that organization. What counts as firsthand evidence? A field report should identify when and where the activity occurred, what was observed, which details came from another party and what the observation cannot establish. Photographs need accurate captions and permission where required. Supplier identities, client details and project results require documented support and permission before publication. Concept imagery and hypothetical examples must not be presented as client work. A Canton Fair preparation guide does not imply attendance. A supplier worksheet does not imply that a supplier has been visited or approved. How can readers request a correction? Email contact@sourcinglabusa.com with the page URL, statement concerned and supporting source if available. Substantive content changes should update the visible modification date. Original publication dates remain part of the article record. The website's educational resources do not replace an agreed quotation, purchase contract, independent inspection or professional determination. mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a sourcing agent and a trading company?

acceptedAnswer.text: An agent acts on your behalf and is paid for the service, while you buy from the factory. acceptedAnswer.text: Minimum order quantities commonly start around 500 units. The real minimum follows the product, material, construction, decoration and the split across sizes or colours, so send the quantity you are considering and it can be reviewed against what the product actually requires.

pages.content: September 14, 2026Alibaba vs a Sourcing Company: Compare the Work and Order TermsBy SourcingLab USADecide between direct supplier sourcing and a product supply partner with a task-ownership matrix, quote comparison and a practical packaging example.Choose between Alibaba and a sourcing company by comparing who will define the product, qualify the supplier, check quotations, approve samples and follow production. Also identify who sells and invoices the goods. A marketplace is a way to find and transact with suppliers; a sourcing company's role depends on its contract. Neither route removes the need for a clear specification. This is a decision framework, not a ranking or a review of individual suppliers. Platform terms change; check Alibaba's own current information and the exact transaction terms before relying on any platform protection. This guide does not promise that a badge, listing or payment method protects every order.Who owns each task in the two routes?Use the table as a worksheet. Replace “confirm” with the actual person's or company's name. Buying through a marketplace does not stop you from appointing separate inspection or logistics providers. Likewise, hiring a sourcing company does not automatically include every service in its product price. TaskDirect supplier purchaseSourcing or product supply arrangementProduct briefYour team prepares and agrees it with the supplierConfirm who prepares it and who approves itCandidate comparisonYour team gathers and evaluates evidenceConfirm the qualification work and its limitsProduct invoiceIdentify the seller in the transactionIdentify whether the partner is agent or sellerSample approvalYour team records accepted features and exceptionsYour team still needs an approval decisionProduction follow-upAssign an internal owner or external providerConfirm checkpoints included in the quoteTesting and inspectionAppoint providers when neededConfirm scope, provider and separate chargesImport and deliveryIdentify responsible parties and costsIdentify responsible parties and costsCorrections or disputesReview supplier contract and applicable platform termsReview the relevant agency or supply contract The useful distinction is the work and commercial arrangement. An agent may charge for coordination while the buyer purchases directly. A product supply business buys and resells under its own agreed terms. Read how these arrangements differ and ask for a written scope rather than inferring it from the label “sourcing company.”When can direct sourcing fit?Direct sourcing can fit when your team can write an actionable brief, assess supplier evidence, manage comparisons, review samples and handle order follow-up. Use a named project owner and preserve the supplier's proposed deviations from the brief. The buyer should know which decisions require external technical or import advice. It may be worth paying for specialist help at a particular stage even if the purchase remains direct. For example, product testing and a production checkpoint answer different questions; do not buy one assuming it covers the other. Use the supplier evidence matrix to identify the gaps first.When can a product supply partner fit?A partner can fit when a project involves several components, repeated specification discussions, sampling decisions or coordination that your team needs help managing. Evaluate the proposal against those tasks. Ask what you receive before ordering, which approvals remain yours, and how product pricing and additional costs are presented. Sourcing Lab USA's current offer is the sourcing, purchase and supply of products, with clothing, textiles and packaging as core specialties. The quotation identifies the company in France or China contracting with you and invoicing the goods. It is not a published commission-based service. See China-to-U.S. product procurement.A packaging comparison you can actually useImagine a U.S. brand needs a printed box, a fitted insert and a label. This is a hypothetical brief, not a client project. Quote A includes the box only; Quote B includes all three components and an assembled sample. Comparing unit prices immediately would hide the scope difference. First, give both bidders the same component list and artwork revision. Second, ask for the same quantity and packing method. Third, list assembly, sample charges, tooling, transport and any excluded costs. Fourth, assign who resolves the fit of the insert around the product. Only then compare totals and the work still left to your team. Our packaging MOQ guide and landed-cost example provide worksheets for those two decisions.Which questions should you ask before choosing?Ask who contracts, who invoices, how proposed substitutions are approved, what the sample proves, which quality checks are included, and who owns unresolved shipment or product requirements. Request the answer in writing. If a proposal cannot answer those questions, record them as open items before making a purchase decision. Compare sourcing fee structures without treating an advertised percentage as a total project cost. For a supply proposal on your own brief, discuss your sourcing project.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

pages.content: September 14, 2026Sourcing Furniture and Building Products from China: The BriefBy SourcingLab USAPrepare a U.S. project sourcing brief for furniture, cabinets, tiles and fixtures, with a specification register and specialist review checkpoints.Start a furniture or building-product sourcing project with a line-item specification, intended installation location, quantities, required documents and named approval responsibilities. A photo and a room count are not enough to compare manufacturers. Confirm the technical, import and installation review for each item before purchasing, especially when several suppliers or product categories must fit the same project. This is an educational brief framework. Sourcing Lab USA's core specialties remain clothing, textiles and packaging. Other categories can be discussed for feasibility; this guide does not establish a completed furniture, construction or hospitality project, a supplier network in those categories, or a guarantee that a proposed item can be supplied.How is a project brief different from a product list?A project brief connects each item to the place it will be used and the requirements it must satisfy there. Give items reference numbers that match drawings, room schedules and sample requests. Identify whether quantities represent pieces, sets, area or another unit. Record who owns the measurements and who approves technical compatibility. For a hotel or restaurant project, separate guest-room, public-area and back-of-house requirements where relevant. A decorative reference can communicate style while leaving cleaning, durability, installation and replacement requirements unresolved. Ask the project team to identify these before asking suppliers to price the item.What information should each category include?Use this matrix to prepare questions for the supplier and the project's qualified designers, installers or product specialists. It is not a list of compliance determinations or services automatically offered by Sourcing Lab USA. CategorySpecification to collectDecision owner to identifyFurnitureDimensions, intended use, construction, materials, finish and assemblyBuyer and responsible designer or specialistKitchen cabinetsDrawing revision, module sizes, hardware, panels and appliance interfacesDesigner and installerBathroom productsDimensions, connection details, materials and intended installationDesigner, installer and relevant specialistTiles and stoneMaterial, dimensions, thickness, finish, intended location and batch requirementsDesigner and installerDoors and windowsOpening schedule, configuration, hardware and required performance evidenceResponsible project professionalLightingIntended location, electrical specification, mounting and required documentationElectrical designer or qualified specialist Confirm the exact products and applicable jurisdiction with those professionals. Do not infer suitability from a product name, export history or an unrelated certificate.Which U.S. product questions need early review?For products containing composite wood, ask whether the item falls within the scope of the EPA's formaldehyde emission standards for composite wood products and which documentation the responsible parties need. This is a review trigger, not a determination that every cabinet or furniture item has the same requirements. For covered consumer products, use the CPSC certification and testing guidance to direct the product-specific review. Local installation and building requirements may require separate review by the responsible project professionals. A supplier's general statement of “U.S. compliance” should be replaced with the exact requirement, applicable product and evidence. Import classification and charges also require a product-specific review. Provide materials, construction, use, origin and pricing to the relevant specialist, using the official U.S. tariff schedule as a reference. Do not apply a generic China tariff percentage to the entire project budget.How do you compare quotations across several suppliers?Use one schedule with item code, specification revision, unit, quantity, included hardware or components, sample scope, packing, price basis and open questions. Keep substitutions visible. A cabinet price excluding hardware or a lighting price excluding a specified component is not directly comparable with a complete-item quote. Then assign ownership of interfaces. Who verifies that a cabinet opening matches the appliance? Who approves the door handing? Who confirms a tile sample's relationship to the production batch? These are original planning questions for the project team, not assurances that a supply partner provides engineering services.How should delivery and installation be planned?Ask for packing details that connect cartons or crates to item references and receiving locations. Confirm who handles consolidation if needed, transport, import arrangements, unloading, storage and installation. These responsibilities and costs must be agreed rather than inferred from a factory quote. Create a receiving sequence based on the actual project plan. Do not use a production estimate as a promised installation date. See the landed-cost worked example for a way to record unknown costs, and the quality checkpoint worksheet for open approval items.What can you send for a feasibility discussion?Send the item schedule, intended U.S. location and use, drawings or references, quantities, budget basis and target dates. Identify the professionals already responsible for technical and import review. Sourcing Lab USA will assess the proposed scope before making a supply proposal; category feasibility is not assumed. Discuss the product requirements. Official references checked September 14, 2026. This guide is procurement preparation, not legal, customs, engineering or product-certification advice.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

Includes a downloadable meeting worksheet.Prepare for Canton Fair by defining the products and requirements you want to discuss, selecting relevant exhibitors, and taking the same RFQ and evidence questions to each meeting. After the fair, compare written responses, verify business identities and review samples before ordering. A productive meeting creates a next decision and evidence request; it does not by itself qualify a supplier. This is a preparation guide, not a report of Sourcing Lab USA attending the fair. No attendance, supplier visit or relationship is claimed. For current registration, event dates and categories, use the official Canton Fair buyer guide and official overseas-buyer attendance information. Confirm the edition and relevant phase before making travel commitments.What should you prepare before visiting?Create a one-page summary for each product and keep the detailed specification available separately. Include the product's intended use, essential materials and dimensions, branding, estimated quantity by variant, target market and sample questions. Mark which details may change if they affect feasibility or cost. Give every brief a reference and revision. Use the same version in comparable conversations. For packaging, include product dimensions and component requirements; for clothing, include the tech pack or a clear statement of which details still need development. Start with the product sourcing brief template.Which questions should you ask at a supplier meeting?Ask how the displayed product relates to the version you need. A display sample may demonstrate a finish without representing your material, dimensions or quantity. Record the answer and the evidence promised, rather than turning the conversation into a confirmed capability claim. QuestionRecord at the meetingFollow-up evidenceWhich company would quote and supply this product?Legal name and contactCompany details and written quotationWhich production steps do you perform?Process and site describedRelevant capability evidenceWhat would change for our specification?Proposed differencesWritten response to the briefWhat sets MOQ for this version?Quantity and variant assumptionsPrice breaks and setup costsWhat would a sample demonstrate?Material, structure and finish scopeSample proposal and approval basisWhich product documents are available?Document names and claimed scopeCopies for appropriate reviewWhat is the next decision?Named contact, action and target dateWritten follow-up Download the Canton Fair meeting worksheet. It includes a field for what you observed yourself versus what a supplier told you.How should you compare suppliers after the fair?Group candidates by product and brief revision. Request written confirmation of the meeting notes before treating them as a quotation. Use the supplier evidence matrix to separate identity, production fit, samples and order terms. Compare quotations only after material, quantity, components and delivery assumptions are aligned. A useful follow-up sequence is: confirm contact and company identity; send the dated brief; record the response and deviations; resolve the highest-impact gaps; then agree the next sampling decision. Do not send a deposit simply because a booth sample looked suitable. Payment and contracting details require their own review.Canton Fair or online sourcing: how do you decide?In-person meetings can support direct product discussions and observation of display samples. Online research can help prepare a shortlist and collect documents before or after a meeting. Both routes still require written specifications, qualification and agreed order terms. Use the direct sourcing versus partner comparison to decide who will perform those tasks. The fair should be one source of candidate information within the procurement process. A large number of business cards is not the same as a set of comparable, qualified proposals.What should a factory visit add?Start with questions a visit can actually answer, such as the production steps relevant to your product, how material and order records are handled, and where your unresolved technical questions can be reviewed. Record the date, location, participants and scope of observation. A hosted visit is not automatically an independent factory audit or proof of future performance. Where a formal audit is required, appoint an appropriate provider and agree its scope. For subsequent production decisions, prepare the quality checkpoint plan.How should genuine field observations be documented?Keep original photographs with dates, permissions and captions explaining what they show. Distinguish observations from supplier claims, and state the limits of a small set of conversations. Avoid presenting a few display products as an industry-wide trend. Obtain permission before publishing identifiable people, supplier details or confidential specifications. Sourcing Lab USA can publish field reports when there is actual activity and supporting evidence. Until then, use this preparation workflow and submit a product brief for a project-specific sourcing discussion. pages.content: September 14, 2026China Sourcing for U.S. Companies: A Decision-by-Decision GuideBy SourcingLab USAFind manufacturers, qualify suppliers and compare quotes using a documented approval workflow, with RFQ, quality and landed-cost resources.To source products from China, define the product and intended U.S. use, identify suitable suppliers, compare written quotations, approve samples, and agree production checkpoints and delivery responsibilities before ordering. Keep a record of the evidence supporting each decision. A supplier listing, a low price or an attractive sample alone does not settle whether an order is ready. This guide is a buying workflow for U.S. brands and business customers. It connects the decisions that often sit in separate emails: the product brief, supplier review, sample approval, price basis and shipment responsibilities. Start with the editable product brief.How do you find manufacturers that fit the product?Search by production requirements, not just the product name. For a printed box, structure, material, print process and assembly may distinguish suitable suppliers. For clothing, fabric, construction, size grading and decoration matter. Create a shortlist from relevant directories, trade events, referrals and direct manufacturer research, then test each candidate against the same brief. Record the source of each lead, the business name, the contact and the reason it appears relevant. Ask which production steps the company performs and which it subcontracts. A factory and a trading company can both be relevant; the decision depends on the proposed arrangement and evidence. Our supplier qualification guide shows what to request before comparing price.What should happen at each sourcing stage?The table below is an original Sourcing Lab USA planning workflow, introduced with this guide. It is a decision aid, not a certification or a claim about completed projects. Assign a person to each open decision rather than assuming the supplier will resolve it. StageDecision to makeRecord to keepSpecificationWhat must the product do, and what may change?Numbered brief and revisionDiscoveryWhich candidates appear to fit the process and quantity?Shortlist with source and production scopeQualificationWhich claims are supported, missing or contradictory?Evidence register and open questionsRFQAre proposals based on the same requirements?Quote comparison and exclusionsSamplesWhich features are approved for production?Sample reference, photographs and approval notesNegotiationWhich changes affect price, MOQ or risk?Written alternatives and revised quotationProductionWhat will be checked, by whom and when?Order-specific checkpoint planReleaseHave discrepancies and required documents been resolved?Release decision and unresolved itemsConsolidation, if relevantCan components be combined under agreed arrangements?Packing list, handoff owner and confirmed costsTransport and receiptWho arranges each step and verifies receipt?Shipping instructions and receiving record These are decision stages, not a promised schedule or a list of services automatically included in a quote. External inspection, testing, consolidation and transport must have an agreed provider and scope when required.What makes two quotations comparable?Use one revision of the RFQ checklist. Separate product price, setup, samples, testing or inspection, and delivery costs. Record quantity by variant, payment terms, quote validity, proposed substitutions and the exact delivery basis. A cheaper quote for a thinner board or a different fabric is an alternative specification, not evidence of a saving. For example, a packaging supplier might quote a box and insert together while another quotes only the box. Add a component-completeness column before comparing their totals. The same principle applies to garment labels, trims and individual packing. Use the landed-cost worked example to keep missing amounts visible.How do U.S. import requirements enter the process?Bring the exact product description, materials, intended use, origin and destination to the relevant import and product specialists before approving production. CBP explains that importer responsibility remains with the importer even when a customs broker is used. A supply quotation should therefore name responsibilities, not leave the importer unspecified. Use the official U.S. tariff schedule as a reference for classification review. This guide does not assign a tariff code or rate. Product requirements and charges depend on the specific goods and current rules; ask a licensed customs broker or qualified product specialist where appropriate.When is using a sourcing partner worthwhile?A partner can be useful when your team needs help turning specifications, supplier discussions, samples and production decisions into an agreed order. Direct sourcing may fit a team with the time and expertise to perform those tasks itself. Compare the actual work, contracting parties and costs in both routes. See Alibaba versus a sourcing company. Sourcing Lab USA is a custom packaging and textile procurement partner for U.S. brands. Its commercial offer is sourcing, purchasing and supplying products through an established independent China partnership. Current quotations identify the contracting and invoicing company in France or China. The Miami expansion is planned for 2027. Read how product supply works or submit your requirements.What should you do when information is missing?Keep the affected decision open. An unverified company identity calls for further qualification; a sample that differs from the drawing calls for a corrected sample or an explicit change approval. A missing transport cost calls for an estimate with an owner and expiry date. Use the quality checkpoint worksheet to connect these open items to the decision they block. External sources checked September 14, 2026. Workflow and examples are editorial planning tools; they do not establish supplier reliability or product compliance.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

pages.content: September 14, 2026China Sourcing Quality Checklist: Samples to Shipment DecisionsBy SourcingLab USACreate order-specific quality checkpoints for packaging and textiles, with a defect log, approval record and downloadable worksheet.A useful sourcing quality checklist links each requirement to an approved specification, a checking method, a responsible party and an action if it fails. Separate sample approval, production follow-up, independent inspection and product testing. They answer different questions. Agree the checks before production so a shipment decision is based on recorded evidence rather than an unqualified statement that quality is acceptable. Download the quality checkpoint worksheet and adapt it to the actual product with the appropriate specialists.What should you approve in the sample?Identify the sample by date, product code and specification revision. List what it represents: material, construction, dimensions, fit, print, decoration or assembly. Record features that still differ from the intended production specification. If a sample uses a substitute material, approval of its shape does not approve that material for production. For packaging, check product fit, opening and closure, insert position, artwork version and packing method. For a garment, use the relevant size measurements, fabric description, seam construction, trims, label artwork and decoration position. Numerical tolerances must come from the agreed specification or qualified technical review, not from a generic checklist.What belongs in the checkpoint plan?CheckpointPackaging exampleTextile exampleRecord requiredBefore productionApproved dieline and print filesApproved tech pack and size breakdownRevision and buyer approvalMaterialsBoard or other material matches the orderFabric and trims match the orderMaterial reference and exceptionsConstructionBox, insert and product fit togetherMeasurements and seams match the specificationMeasurement or review notesBrandingCorrect artwork, color reference and copyCorrect label and decoration placementApproved reference and photographsPackingComponent count and carton planSize/color assortment and individual packingPacking list and carton identificationBefore releaseOpen issues resolved or heldOpen issues resolved or heldWritten decision and responsible person The table is a starting point. Product-specific tests, test equipment, sampling plans, acceptance criteria and inspection scope need separate agreement. Do not present “AQL passed” as meaningful without the actual plan, defect definitions and report.How should you document a defect or discrepancy?Use one issue record per discrepancy. Include the requirement, observed difference, evidence, affected units or scope if known, proposed correction, owner and review date. Assign an outcome such as hold, rework and recheck, or approved change. Record who has authority to make that decision. Hypothetical example: an assembled packaging sample closes only when the insert is compressed. The requirement is a box that closes with the agreed product and insert. The issue record should reference the sample and dimensions, request a corrected component or specification, and require a new fit review. A photograph of an empty closed box would not resolve this particular issue. Keep correction approval separate from permission to ship. Where the affected scope is unknown, record that uncertainty instead of marking the entire lot as checked.What is a pre-shipment inspection?A pre-shipment inspection examines goods before dispatch against an agreed scope. Ask the appointed provider to state the product reference, lot readiness, sampling basis, checks, limitations and findings. Agree in advance who reviews the report and authorizes release. An inspection covering sampled appearance and dimensions does not itself establish every legal or safety requirement for the product. Sourcing Lab USA's quality follow-up means production coordination and order-specific checkpoints. It is not an independent certified inspection organization. When a project needs independent inspection or testing, identify the external provider, its scope and the related cost in the project arrangements.How are product safety documents different from quality checks?Treat product safety review as its own workstream. For example, CPSC explains that certification and testing requirements depend on the covered product and applicable rules in its general-use product guidance. Do not assume an appearance check or supplier's generic report satisfies those requirements. Ask the relevant specialist to confirm what applies to your actual item and shipment. For textile labels, use the U.S. textile planning guide. For supplier evidence before sampling, use the qualification matrix.What should you keep after delivery?Compare the receiving record with the approved order and packing list. Preserve issue evidence, the agreed response and the final resolution. Feed changes into the next specification revision so a repeat order does not depend on someone remembering an email. Start the commercial discussion with custom packaging, clothing and textiles, or how we work. Use a quote-completeness worksheet instead of assuming a universal sourcing fee.A sourcing agent's cost depends on the work agreed and how the provider charges for it. A proposal may use a fixed project fee, an order-based commission, a retainer or a product resale price. Compare the total quoted scope, exclusions and payment basis. A percentage alone does not tell you whether samples, inspection, transport or supplier follow-up are included. Sourcing Lab USA quotes the purchase and supply of products. It does not publish a universal agency commission. The company contracting and invoicing from France or China is identified in the quotation. This article explains ways to compare offers; it does not introduce a new paid consulting service.How do the pricing arrangements differ?Ask the provider to describe its actual arrangement. The table identifies questions to resolve, not market-average prices or legal definitions of every contract. Quoted basisQuestion to resolveUseful comparisonFixed project feeWhich deliverables and revisions are included?Total fee plus excluded workPercentage of order valueWhich amount is the percentage applied to?Fee base, minimum fee and excluded chargesRetainerWhich work and period does it cover?Monthly scope, capacity and exit termsProduct resale priceWhich goods and order responsibilities are included?Like-for-like product and delivered-cost basis A quoted fee based on goods value differs from one based on goods plus transport. Ask about minimum charges, repeat orders, samples, tooling, supplier rebates or other compensation relevant to the arrangement. Record what the provider discloses rather than assuming that a low visible fee means a lower total cost.What does a useful cost comparison look like?Start with one specification revision and quantity. Give each amount one of four states: quoted, estimated, excluded, or unknown. An unknown cost is not zero. A cost explicitly excluded from one quote still belongs in the comparison if your project requires it. Illustrative arithmetic only: suppose a hypothetical agency proposal quotes $8,000 for goods and a 6% fee on goods value. The fee is $480, making the subtotal $8,480 before any other costs. Suppose a separate supply proposal quotes $8,700 for the goods and agreed coordination. You cannot conclude which is cheaper without comparing samples, setup, quality scope, transport, and the work remaining to the buyer. Do not treat an informal sample discussion as acceptance of a production order. Use the RFQ checklist to standardize the information supplied to each bidder. Then use the landed-cost worksheet to separate the product decision from shipment and import estimates.How should you compare the time your team will spend?List the buyer tasks that remain: preparing artwork, reviewing samples, answering supplier questions, arranging specialists and approving changes. Estimate time for your own internal planning without presenting it as a supplier charge or guaranteed saving. A partner can reduce the coordination your team needs to perform only to the extent that its agreed scope actually covers that work. For a component-heavy packaging project, the more useful negotiation may be a clearer assembly sample and approval process rather than a lower percentage. For apparel, it may be consolidating comments on fit, fabric and labels into a single revision. Discuss these outputs before comparing fee headlines.Does Sourcing Lab USA charge a sourcing-agent fee?The current commercial offer is a quotation for product sourcing, purchase and supply. pages.content: September 14, 2026How to Verify a Chinese Supplier: Evidence and ScorecardBy SourcingLab USAA supplier qualification matrix that separates identity, capability, samples and order terms. Download the evidence worksheet before approving an order.Verify a Chinese supplier by checking the legal business identity, matching it to the proposed contracting and payment parties, assessing product-specific manufacturing capability, and reviewing samples and commercial terms. Treat these as separate checks. Registration can help establish who a business is; it does not prove that it can produce your specification or perform your order reliably. The Sourcing Lab Supplier Evidence Matrix below is an original editorial worksheet, introduced on September 14, 2026. It is not an industry standard, an audit certificate or a list of approved factories. Download the blank supplier evidence worksheet.What company information should you request?Request the Chinese legal name, Unified Social Credit Code, business license details, registered address, proposed production site, and the name of the entity issuing the quotation. Compare the business identity against the official National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System. Its regional portal supports searches by enterprise name, credit code or registration number. Access may require interactive verification or local assistance. Record the source and date of the check. Keep the legal name separate from an English trading name or marketplace display name. If the supplier, exporter, seller or bank beneficiary differs, ask for a documented explanation and have the arrangement reviewed before payment. Do not publish sensitive business or banking documents in a public scorecard.What evidence belongs in a supplier scorecard?Use one row per question, with a document reference and named reviewer. Mark evidence as missing, supplier-provided, cross-checked, or contradictory. Cross-checked means compared with another relevant source; it does not mean risk-free. AreaEvidence to requestWhat it can supportWhat remains unresolvedIdentityLegal name, registration identifier, quotation entityThe identity being proposedWhether the order will be performedProduction fitProcess description, proposed site, subcontracted stepsA capability discussion for this productWhether stated capacity is availableSpecificationWritten response to the same brief revisionWhich requirements the supplier acceptsWhether production will match themSamplesIdentified sample with measured review notesSelected appearance, dimensions and constructionConsistency across the production lotTest documentsReport identity, issuer, date, product and scopeEvidence relevant to the tested itemApplicability to changed materials or modelsCommercial termsSeller, price basis, payment and delivery termsResponsibilities proposed for the orderAmbiguities requiring contract reviewIssue handlingWritten correction and escalation processA proposed way to handle discrepanciesHow a real dispute will be resolved Do not give a missing document a positive status because the supplier responded quickly. Responsiveness is useful, but it answers a different question from technical suitability.How can you score the completeness of a review?For internal planning, count the required questions with a recorded answer and supporting evidence, then divide by the total required questions. If 9 of 12 have that evidence, the file is 75% complete. That number describes documentation coverage only: it is not a 75% probability of a safe order and cannot override a serious contradiction. Identify critical questions before requesting quotes. Examples include the identity of the seller, whether a sample meets a non-negotiable requirement, and who owns an unresolved import review. Keep the order decision on hold when a critical answer is missing or contradictory, even if the rest of the file is complete. If a requirement does not apply, record the reason and reviewer instead of silently deleting it.Factory or trading company: which is better?Neither label decides the result. A trading company may coordinate several processes; a manufacturer may subcontract a specific finish. Ask who performs each step, who sells to you, what changes require approval, and what evidence is available. Compare the proposed arrangement using the agent and supplier explanation, then evaluate the actual product against the RFQ. As an illustrative example, a box supplier may provide its own printing but buy inserts elsewhere. That is a question about coordination and component approval, not automatic proof of a problem. Request a complete assembly sample and identify who resolves a fit mismatch between the box and insert.When do you need an independent inspection or specialist?Request an independent provider when the decision requires site verification, a formal inspection report, laboratory testing or specialized technical judgment beyond the available evidence. Agree its scope, limitations, product reference and reporting requirements. A video call or production photo should not be described as an independent certified inspection. Sourcing Lab USA provides sourcing and product supply with order-specific production coordination. This educational guide does not advertise a standalone factory audit or certification service. For the production handoff, use the quality control checklist and documented sourcing method.What should you recheck before a repeat order?Reconfirm the contracting and payment parties, specification revision, production site or process changes, materials, sample basis and delivery terms. Keep changes in a revision log. A previous order or an old test report does not resolve every question about a new product or changed material. Official registry interfaces checked September 14, 2026; no supplier was investigated or certified for this article. pages.content: September 7, 2026China Sourcing RFQ Checklist: How to Prepare a Product BriefBy Gregory BaranesPrepare a China sourcing quotation request with product specs, quantities, samples and delivery requirements. Includes a free brief template.A useful China sourcing request for quotation (RFQ) identifies the product, intended use, specifications, quantity by variant, sample requirements, destination and target date. Separate requirements you must keep from details you can change. This gives the supplier or product supply partner a clear basis for assessing feasibility and preparing a proposal. Download the free product sourcing brief template. Fill in what you know and mark unresolved details as “to confirm.” The template works for clothing, packaging and other products submitted for feasibility review.What should a sourcing brief include?Give each product its own reference number. Include these details in the same document: Product and use: what it is, who will use it, and how it will be sold or used. Reference material: drawings, photographs, a tech pack, a dieline or an existing sample. Identify which details are for inspiration and which must be reproduced. Specification: materials, dimensions, colors, construction, decoration and packaging. State units and tolerances where known. Quantity: total units and the breakdown by style, size, color, artwork or other variant. Separate a first order from a possible repeat order. Sample review: which features need approval before production and who will approve them. Commercial target: budget, currency and what you expect that budget to include. Mark estimates clearly. Destination and timing: delivery location, target arrival date, and whether that date is flexible. Required documentation: documents or product claims your team needs to review before approving the order. Do not fill gaps with guesses. An unanswered specification is something to resolve; an incorrect specification can become the basis of a quotation.What is different for clothing and textiles?For a garment, include front and back drawings, a size chart, fabric composition and weight, color references, stitching, trims, labels and decoration placement. Break quantities down by size and color. Say whether a reference garment represents the fit, the fabric, the finish, or all three. For a tote bag or another textile item, dimensions, construction, intended use and decoration may matter more than a garment size chart. A reference photo alone rarely describes every detail needed for production. The apparel tech pack and MOQ guide explains how to discuss materials and order quantities. See the clothing and textile sourcing page for the product scope.What is different for custom packaging?Start with the product being packed. Include its dimensions, weight, fragility, presentation needs and intended packing method. Specify whether box measurements are internal or external. If you have a dieline, include its revision and the artwork files associated with it. Describe the structure, material, print, finish, inserts and closure. State whether different artwork versions share the same structure. Ask for a sample that lets you check product fit as well as appearance. Explore custom packaging sourcing, private label packaging and the packaging MOQ guide.How do you compare product quotations?Compare proposals against the same brief and revision. For each quotation, record the unit price, quantity, included materials and finishes, sample charges, setup or tooling costs, payment terms, quotation validity and delivery basis. Ask what is excluded. Check whether an alternative material, different quantity or simpler finish explains a price difference. Keep proposed substitutions separate from the original specification until you approve them. Sample timing, production timing and transport timing should be identified separately. A production estimate alone does not confirm the date goods will arrive at your destination. For a cost worksheet, use the landed-cost planning guide.What should be confirmed before production?Keep an approval record linking the final specification, approved sample, quantity breakdown and commercial terms. Identify the production checkpoints, how changes will be approved and who is responsible for each delivery step. Requirements for testing, documentation or import review depend on the exact product and should be settled with the appropriate parties before the order proceeds. A quotation request is the start of a conversation. It is not an order confirmation, a fixed price or a guarantee that a product can be supplied.How will Sourcing Lab USA use your brief?Sourcing Lab USA accepts China sourcing projects now, with invoicing from France or China as identified in the quotation. Clothing, textiles and packaging are the core specialties; other products are assessed on request through an established independent China sourcing partnership. The quotation identifies the company in France or China purchasing, supplying and invoicing the products, along with the commercial terms. The brief helps define what can be proposed, sampled and agreed before an order. Read about China-to-U.S. product sourcing and supply, or send your project brief. If you are still deciding who to work with, what a sourcing agent does and how buying and supplying differs covers the arrangements on offer before you send a brief.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

pages.content: September 3, 2026Apparel Sourcing: Understanding Tech Packs and MOQBy Gregory BaranesUpdated September 8, 2026Learn why a clear tech pack is essential for negotiating Minimum Order Quantities (MOQ) and defining product requirements when sourcing custom textiles.When U.S. brands start sourcing custom apparel and textiles from China, two terms immediately dominate the conversation: Tech Packs and MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity). A tech pack records the product specification; MOQ is the minimum quantity quoted for a particular product or variant. Review them together, because materials, colors, construction and setup requirements can affect the quantity a supplier can propose.What is a Tech Pack?A Tech Pack (Technical Packet) is the blueprint for your textile product. It is a comprehensive document that contains every detail a factory needs to manufacture your garment or textile item. A standard tech pack includes: Technical Sketches: Flat drawings of the front, back, and details. Bill of Materials (BOM): A list of all fabrics, threads, buttons, zippers, and labels required. Measurements and Grading: Exact dimensions for every size you plan to produce. Construction Details: Stitching types, seam finishes, and placement of labels. Colorways: Specific Pantone codes or color references. Why the Tech Pack Dictates the MOQMany brands ask, "What is your standard MOQ?" before providing any product details. The reality is that for custom textiles, the MOQ is rarely a fixed number—it is determined by the details in your tech pack. Here is why: Fabric Minimums (MOQ of the Mill): If your tech pack specifies a custom-dyed fabric or a unique blend, the factory must purchase that fabric from a mill. Ask whether fabric minimums apply to the proposed material and color, and how those minimums affect the garment quantity. Setup Costs: Custom hardware (like branded zippers) or complex printing (like all-over sublimation) requires significant setup time. Factories require higher MOQs to absorb these setup costs. How to Lower Your MOQ Using Your Tech PackIf you are a startup or testing a new product line, you likely want to keep your MOQ as low as possible. You can design your tech pack strategically to achieve this: Use Available Market Fabrics: Instead of custom-dying a fabric to a specific Pantone color, ask your sourcing partner to find an "available market fabric" (in-stock fabric) that closely matches your requirement. This may change the minimum commitment; availability and quantities still need confirmation. Standardize Hardware: Use standard buttons and zippers rather than custom-molded hardware. Consolidate Colors: Launch with one or two core colors rather than five different colorways. MOQs are often calculated per color, per style. The Importance of a Clear BriefA detailed tech pack helps identify assumptions before an order is approved. When a factory has to guess your requirements, they price in risk, which often results in higher costs and stricter MOQs. By presenting a professional, complete specification, you demonstrate that you are a serious buyer, which can give you more leverage during negotiations. Sourcing projects are available now, with contracting and invoicing from France or China as identified in your quotation. Explore clothing and textile sourcing, or use the China sourcing RFQ checklist and free brief template to prepare a project discussion. For the specification side of a garment project, clothing and textile sourcing covers fabric, construction, sizing and branding in detail.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

A material name or natural-looking finish is not enough to substantiate an environmental benefit.Start with the goal and the productRecord the product dimensions, weight, protection needs, presentation requirements and how the customer will use the packaging. Then identify the environmental objective. Keep product protection and the intended packing process in the brief so proposed changes can be assessed against both. For example, you might ask to compare a current box and insert with a revised structure using fewer separate components. This is a comparison request, not a promise of reduced environmental impact or lower delivery costs.Specify the whole packaging structureList the board or paper, coatings, laminations, inks, adhesive, closures and inserts. Ask suppliers to identify proposed substitutions. Compare the complete construction; one component does not describe the finished package. For recycled-content requirements, state the component the requirement applies to and request the supporting documentation. Keep certification requests specific to the material, supplier and production route being proposed.Check the claim before printing itThe FTC Green Guides summary cautions against broad, unqualified environmental benefit claims and explains how specific claims need support. Recyclability and recycled content are different claims; do not treat one as proof of the other. Before adding an environmental statement to artwork, obtain an appropriate review of the wording and evidence. Describe which part of the product or package the statement covers. Sourcing Lab USA does not act as a certification body.Compare samples and commercial termsReview product fit, assembly, appearance and protection using the agreed sample process. For each option, record the dimensions, materials, unit price, quantity, setup charges and packing details. Ask how a proposed change affects the specification and shipment configuration rather than assuming savings. Keep the final material specification, supporting documents and artwork approval together. If any component changes before production, review whether the original claim and approval still apply.Prepare a packaging sourcing requestSourcing Lab USA welcomes product sourcing projects now, with invoicing from France or China as confirmed in the quotation. A clear brief helps assess custom packaging options through its independent China sourcing partnership. Material choices, samples, documentation and commercial terms are confirmed per project. Explore custom packaging sourcing, private label packaging, or use the downloadable sourcing brief. FTC guidance checked on September 7, 2026. Confirm current requirements before using environmental claims. pages.content: August 28, 2026Custom Packaging MOQ: How to Plan a First Production RunBy Gregory BaranesUpdated September 14, 2026 by SourcingLab USAUnderstand the factors that shape a custom packaging minimum order quantity and the information to confirm before you request a quote.The minimum order quantity (MOQ) is the smallest production quantity a supplier will accept for a specific quotation. In custom packaging, ask whether it applies per structure, material, artwork or finished item. Setup, print, finish, tooling and variant splits can change the minimum. Compare the complete order commitment and the stock you can use, not just the unit price. The most useful starting point is a clear brief rather than a target quantity in isolation.Why MOQs varyCustom packaging may require setup steps before the first production unit is made. Depending on the project, these can include artwork preparation, color matching, printing setup, cutting or forming tools, material purchasing, and hand assembly. A supplier needs a production run that makes those steps viable. Two boxes that look similar can have very different MOQs if one uses standard dimensions and a simple print while the other needs a new structure, special material, detailed finish, or several assembly steps.Questions to include in your RFQAsk the supplier to state: MOQ for the quoted specification; price breaks at practical quantities; one-time tooling or setup charges; sample cost and timing; included and excluded finishing steps; carton details, production lead time, and shipping terms. Ways to explore a lower commitmentIf the first MOQ is too high for the project, consider options that preserve the product objective: Use a standard structure or size where it still protects the product. Compare a simpler finish or printing method with the initial concept. Separate the first sample run from production quantities. Ask for quantity breakpoints and compare total order cost, not only unit price. Sourcing Lab USA can review a custom packaging brief, including the specification, estimated quantity, sample needs, and delivery destination, before coordinating supplier proposals. The final MOQ and commercial terms are confirmed for each order. For a complete packaging brief, see custom packaging for U.S. brands.Is MOQ per order, per design or per component?Ask the supplier to identify the unit behind each minimum. A box, insert and label may have different production requirements. Several artwork versions can share a structure while still requiring separate print setups. A total of 2,000 boxes does not necessarily satisfy a 500-unit minimum for each of five distinct versions. QuestionWhy it affects the commitmentDoes MOQ apply per structure or artwork?Shared dimensions may not combine separate print runsCan variants share material or tooling?A common input may change the quoted basisAre inserts and labels included?Component minimums may exceed the assembled-unit quantityAre samples part of the production quantity?Do not count them unless the quotation doesCan repeat orders use the same setup?Confirm retained tooling, revision and costsA hypothetical first-order comparisonAssume a buyer is comparing two fictional quotes for the same packaging specification. Option A is 500 units at $2.80 plus $150 setup; Option B is 1,000 units at $2.10 plus the same setup. Neither quote is a Sourcing Lab USA offer or an industry benchmark. OptionGoods and setup onlyAllocated cost per ordered unitA: 500 units$1,550$3.10B: 1,000 units$2,250$2.25 Option B has a lower unit cost but requires $700 more for this scope and 500 additional units. If the buyer can use only 500 units before the artwork changes, the extra stock matters. Both comparisons still exclude transport, import and other order-specific costs; use the landed-cost worksheet before deciding.How can you negotiate without weakening the brief?Separate non-negotiable requirements from optional finishes. Request a written alternative for a standard structure, fewer artwork versions, shared materials or a simpler finish, then compare the revised specification and total commitment. Avoid agreeing to an unspecified substitution solely to meet a target MOQ. Record each alternative with its quantity, unit price, setup, sample scope, packing and expiry. A small sample run does not automatically prove that the same economics or process applies to production. Review sample and quality checkpoints before ordering.What does Sourcing Lab USA indicate for planning?The website's owner-confirmed planning figures use 500 units as a common starting point, subject to the product, material, construction, decoration and variant split. It is not a universal minimum or a promise that every 500-unit brief is feasible. Your quotation confirms the actual MOQ and order terms. Send the packaging details and quantity you are considering. When your quantities are settled, custom packaging sourcing from China sets out the materials, print finishes and specification a quotation needs.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

pages.content: August 25, 2026How to Discuss Material Claims When Sourcing Custom TextilesBy Gregory BaranesUpdated August 31, 2026A practical way to define textile material requirements, request supporting documents, and avoid making claims that the order cannot substantiate.When a custom textile project includes organic, recycled, or other material claims, the specification has to be more precise than a marketing phrase. The fiber blend, construction, color, trims, labels, intended use, and documentation requirements can all affect the supplier options, sampling process, price, and lead time. This article is a sourcing checklist, not a certification or compliance opinion. Requirements should be assessed for the particular product and market before production.Start with a material briefDescribe the product in a way that a supplier can quote consistently: fiber composition and target weight; weave, knit, construction, size, and tolerances; color, printing, embroidery, labels, and trims; intended use and target market; quantity, target delivery date, and any documents the buyer needs to review. Compare like-for-like optionsMaterial choices can change the cost, minimum order quantity, performance, appearance, and production lead time. Instead of assuming a fixed premium, request comparable proposals for the same specification and quantity. Make clear which elements are mandatory and which can be adjusted after sampling.Request documentation before making a claimIf a buyer intends to make a certification, recycled-content, organic-content, or safety claim, request the relevant documentation from the proposed supplier and check that its scope and validity match the material and production route being quoted. Examples that may be relevant depending on the product include GOTS, GRS, and OEKO-TEX® STANDARD 100. Do not assume that a document applies to every component of a finished product. Where a claim matters commercially, obtain appropriate professional advice and retain the documents required for the order.Use sampling to confirm the productSampling is where the material hand feel, color, construction, print, trims, labeling, and packaging can be reviewed against the agreed brief. Record approved changes before production so that the final specification and commercial terms stay aligned. Sourcing Lab USA coordinates custom textile procurement around the specific brief, supplier proposal, samples, and agreed production follow-up. Documentation, quality checkpoints, shipping terms, and importer responsibilities are agreed case by case; the company does not represent itself as a certification body, testing laboratory, or customs adviser. Learn how to prepare a custom textile product brief before requesting a proposal. To turn a material preference into a garment specification, see clothing and textile sourcing.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

pages.content: August 20, 2026How to Plan Landed Costs for Custom Packaging and Textile OrdersBy Gregory BaranesUpdated September 14, 2026 by SourcingLab USAA practical checklist of the cost items to confirm before ordering custom packaging or textiles from China to the United States.Landed cost combines the goods price with the order-specific costs of bringing the goods to an agreed destination. For a packaging or textile purchase, list product cost, setup, transport, insurance where applicable, import charges and final delivery. Mark missing amounts as unknown, avoid counting included costs twice, and allocate the total over a clearly stated quantity. The exact items, rates, and party responsible depend on the product, origin, Incoterm, shipment method, importer of record, and destination. Treat this as a planning checklist, not a customs or tax determination. Download the quotation and landed-cost worksheet. It records the source, date, expiry, responsible party and status of each amount so an estimate cannot silently become a confirmed price.What is Landed Cost?The landed cost is the combined cost of the goods and the services required to bring them to the delivery point agreed in the order. It should be calculated against the same quantity and delivery terms as the supplier quote. The Landed Cost Formula Landed Cost = Product cost + International transport + Insurance (if applicable) + Import charges + U.S. handling/delivery + Order-specific costs Before approving a production run, ask for each item to be shown separately whenever possible.1. Product and production costsConfirm the unit price, quantity, tooling or setup, sample charges, artwork changes, packaging of the finished goods, payment terms, and the Incoterm. A lower unit price can be less useful if it excludes an essential cost or only applies to a different specification.2. Transport and insuranceRequest a transport quote that matches the final carton count, dimensions, weight, pickup point, delivery point, and preferred shipping method. For both packaging and textiles, the way goods are packed can materially affect the chargeable volume. Insurance and delivery services should be stated separately if they are not included.3. Classification and import chargesProduct classification, duty treatment, tariffs, and import responsibilities must be checked against the exact product and current rules. The U.S. International Trade Commission's HTS is the official tariff schedule; when binding guidance is required, U.S. Customs and Border Protection explains how to request a classification ruling through its eRulings process. Do not rely on a generic rate or an AI estimate for an import decision. Confirm the classification, applicable charges, and importer obligations for the specific order. A customs broker may be used, but CBP notes that the importer remains responsible for the entry information and duties even when a broker is involved. See CBP's explanation of importer responsibility. Confirm the current treatment of the specific product and shipment with the responsible professional; the example below deliberately supplies no tariff percentage.4. U.S. handling and order-specific costsDepending on the agreed route and terms, the budget may also include port or terminal handling, domestic delivery, storage, inspections arranged by the buyer, or other order-specific services. These should be confirmed in the commercial terms rather than assumed.A practical review before you orderFor each project, build one written cost sheet showing what is included, excluded, estimated, and still to be verified. Sourcing Lab USA can review the product brief, specifications, sample needs, and supplier proposal for packaging and textile projects. Import, delivery, and compliance responsibilities are confirmed in the order-specific commercial terms. For project scope and order terms, see China-to-U.S. packaging and textile procurement.A worked example with unknown import chargesThe following figures are fictional USD amounts for explaining the arithmetic. They are not a quote, market-average costs, a previous order or a tariff estimate. Assume 2,000 units and that no listed amount is already included in another line. Cost inputHypothetical amountBasis to confirm on a real orderGoods: 2,000 × $2.40$4,800Same specification and quantitySetup allocated to this order$300Whether already included in product priceOrigin handling and international transport$1,100Final packing and routeInsurance$60Coverage and inclusionDestination handling and delivery$500Named delivery point and servicesImport chargesUnknown: DProduct-specific professional reviewTotal before unresolved import charges$6,760Not a complete landed cost The planning expression is ($6,760 + D) ÷ 2,000 = $3.38 + D ÷ 2,000 per unit. Additional costs identified during the review must also be added. The unresolved amount is visible instead of being silently treated as zero. As a sensitivity exercise only, adding a fictional $800 cost allowance increases the planning amount by $0.40 per unit. That allowance is not a calculated duty or evidence that $800 covers the import charges. Replace it with confirmed inputs before relying on the budget.How do you avoid double counting and misleading unit costs?Use the delivery basis of the supplier quote to identify which transport and handling charges are already included. The ICC's Incoterms guidance explains the allocation of cost, risk and obligations. Record the chosen rule, named place and edition with the quote. A trade-term abbreviation alone should not replace a complete discussion of the order. Keep order quantity and expected usable quantity separate. In the fictional example, a planning scenario allocating $6,760 over 1,900 usable units gives about $3.56 per unit before D. This is a sensitivity scenario, not an expected defect rate. It demonstrates why the denominator must be stated. For several products, record the allocation method for shared freight or setup. An allocation by quantity may differ from one by volume or weight. Select a method appropriate to the decision and use it consistently across proposals.What makes a cost sheet ready for a decision?Every required amount should have a value or a clearly recorded unresolved item, an inclusion check, a source date and a responsible person. Check quotation validity and confirm changes to materials, packing or route before accepting the total. The RFQ checklist and fee comparison guide help align proposals before this calculation. External sources rechecked September 14, 2026. The arithmetic is an original planning example, not customs, tax or financial advice for a specific order. Landed cost depends on what you are buying and on what terms — China-to-U.S. procurement sets out how those terms are confirmed per order.Sources, examples and corrections · All sourcing resources

pages.content: FREE TEMPLATE · NO EMAIL REQUIREDThe product sourcing briefa supplier can actually quote.A product sourcing brief is the document a supplier quotes from. It states the product, the reference it must match, materials, dimensions, quantity by variant, sample and approval requirements, destination and target date, and separates what is mandatory from what can change. Anything unresolved is marked "to confirm" rather than guessed, because a guessed figure produces a quotation for the wrong product.Download the templateRead it on this pagePlain text, so it opens anywhere and pastes into an email. No sign-up, no tracking, nothing to accept.WHAT THE TEMPLATE ASKS FORSix sections, in the order a supplier reads them.Business and contactCompanyContact nameEmailProduct reference, brief revision and dateProductProduct descriptionIntended use and intended customerReference images, drawings, tech pack or dielineDetails that must match the referenceMaterials and compositionDimensions, units and tolerancesColours, artwork and finishesLabels, trims and packagingMandatory requirementsOptions open to changeQuantityFirst-order quantityBreakdown by size, style, colour or artworkPossible repeat quantity, as an estimate onlySamples and approvalSamples neededFeatures to reviewPerson approving the sampleDocuments or claims to reviewCommercial and deliveryBudget and currencyItems expected within the budgetDelivery destinationTarget arrival date and flexibilityProposed delivery terms, to confirmImport and delivery responsibilities, to confirmQuestions to resolveOutstanding specificationsProduct feasibilityMinimum order quantity by variantUnit price, sample and setup chargesQuotation validity and payment termsSample, production and transport timingProduction checkpoints and change approvalsWHAT TO PLAN AROUNDFigures to hold in mind while you fill it in.Minimum order quantityFrom 500 unitsA common starting point. The real minimum follows the product, material, construction, decoration and the split across sizes or colours.Samples1 to 2 weeksOnce the specification is agreed. A new mould, tooling or a custom material extends it, and a revised sample restarts the cycle.Production45 to 60 daysAfter sample approval, before shipping. Quantity, decoration and factory loading at the time of order all move it.Indicative planning figures, not commitments. The quantity, sampling scope and production timing for your project are confirmed in your quotation.WHAT MAKES A BRIEF UNANSWERABLEFour gaps that send a quotation off course.A quantity with no breakdownFive thousand units across one size behaves nothing like five thousand across six sizes and three colours. The breakdown is what decides whether a minimum is reachable.A reference with no boundaryAttaching a reference product without saying which parts must match leaves the supplier to guess. State what is fixed and what is open.A guessed figure instead of "to confirm"A placeholder dimension or material is treated as a requirement and quoted against. Marking it unresolved costs nothing and avoids a quotation for the wrong product.A claim with no evidence pathA performance, safety or compliance requirement needs to say what evidence will be accepted. It cannot be assumed from a fabric name or a reference product.QUESTIONS, ANSWEREDAbout the brief.What is a product sourcing brief?It is the document a supplier quotes from. It states the product, the reference it must match, materials and dimensions, quantity by variant, sample and approval requirements, destination and target date, and separates mandatory requirements from details that can change.What is the difference between a brief and an RFQ?In practice they are the same document seen from two sides. The brief describes the product you want made; the request for quotation asks a supplier what that product costs and how long it takes. One well-written brief serves as the RFQ.How complete does a brief need to be before sending it?It does not need to be complete. Mark what is unresolved as "to confirm" and send it. An incomplete brief with honest gaps gets a useful first answer; a brief filled with guessed figures gets a quotation for a product you did not intend.What quantities and timing should I plan around?As an indication, minimum order quantities commonly start around 500 units, samples take one to two weeks once the specification is agreed, and production runs about 45 to 60 days after sample approval. All three depend on the product and are confirmed in the quotation.

pages.content: Privacy noticeThis page explains what we collect when you use this website, why we collect it, where it is stored, and how to have it removed. Last updated 14 September 2026.What we collectWhen you send a project brief we collect your name, email address, the type of product you need, an approximate quantity, the page you sent the brief from, and — if you choose to provide them — your company name and a description of your project. Optional project details include purchasing budget, target market or delivery destination, customization, current supplier status and timing. These are included with your project brief.If you join the product update list we collect your email address and the sourcing role you select.We do not ask for payment details, identity documents, or any special category of personal data anywhere on this site.Why we collect itA project brief is used to answer your request: to confirm what can be quoted and sampled, to ask for anything missing, and to reply to you by email. Product update registrations are used only to send occasional updates about the service.We do not sell your information, we do not share it with advertising networks, and we do not add you to a marketing sequence because you sent a brief.Where it is storedBriefs and product update registrations are stored in a Supabase database that only our servers can reach. Brief submissions are also delivered to us as a notification through Netlify Forms, the service that hosts this website.We use Google Analytics to understand how the site is used — which pages are visited and which actions are taken, such as opening or submitting the brief form. Google Analytics sets cookies in your browser and processes this data on Google's infrastructure. It does not receive the contents of your brief.These providers operate in the United States and elsewhere, so your information may be processed outside your country.How long we keep itWe keep a project brief for as long as it takes to answer it and to maintain a record of the conversation, and product update registrations until you ask to be removed. You can ask us to delete either at any time.Your choicesYou can ask for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. Write to contact@sourcinglabusa.com and we will action it.You can block analytics cookies in your browser settings or with a content blocker. The site works normally without them.ContactQuestions about this notice go to contact@sourcinglabusa.com.Back to the brief form
